name: AzuLux Sea Spa, Inc (Mobile Massage)
fail_reason: Below the hard minimum of 5 real, non-stock, non-flyer photos (FORGE-BRIEF 0.b / Puerta de calidad). Exhaustive research performed (see notes), but every image found is either a 2010s-era marketing flyer/graphic with text overlays and stock-style photography, or an unrelated therapist's professional headshot. No Instagram, no Facebook, no usable gallery/work photos exist for this specific business listing. Not a research_degradado case: Google Maps photo cycle, WebSearch, Birdeye, MassageBook and HealthProfs were all checked directly.
address: 7330 Ocean Ter, Miami Beach, FL 33141, United States (Saint Tropez Ocean Front Condominium per GBP - likely the incall/home-base address of a MOBILE massage team, not a public storefront)
address_source: Google Business Profile, cross-confirmed by Birdeye listing (7330 Ocean Terrace, Miami Beach, FL 33141)
phone_source: Google Business Profile, matches the phone printed on the business's own promotional flyer image (gmaps-7.jpg) next to LeticiaD@azulux.com
has_own_site_evidence: The business's OWN promotional flyer (gmaps-7.jpg, a photo on their own Google Business listing) prints the email LeticiaD@azulux.com and references www.azulux.com, and the Birdeye listing explicitly lists Website: https://azulux.com/ as their site. Checked azulux.com directly: curl -I and curl -L both return HTTP 200, but the page is a client-side JS redirect to /lander, which loads GoDaddy's parking-lander infrastructure (img1.wsimg.com/parking-lander, window._trfd.push({ap:'parking'})). This confirms azulux.com is an EXPIRED/LAPSED domain now squatted by a domain parking service, not a live business website. So: no functioning own website exists today, but they clearly had one in the past under this exact domain. This is a strong 'your old website expired, here's a fresh one' outreach angle for whenever usable photos are found.

social_media.evidence: WebSearch '"AzuLux Sea Spa" Miami Beach massage instagram facebook' and '"AzuLux" Miami massage Leticia Diana' returned no Facebook or Instagram profile for this business. Only directory/review listings surfaced (Birdeye, MassageBook therapist profile, HealthProfs therapist profile, Airbnb Experiences for an unrelated 'Leticia' massage listing not clearly tied to this business).

email_source: Visible as plain text printed on the business's own promotional flyer image, downloaded directly from their Google Business Profile photo gallery (output/azuluxseaspa/assets/raw/gmaps-7.jpg), alongside the same phone number used throughout this research. NOT used for outreach in this run per task rules (no contact with businesses), but logged here as a verified real contact.

google_business.profile_url_note: Public Google Maps place link used for this research (no business.google.com vanity URL surfaced): https://www.google.com/maps/place/AzuLux+Sea+Spa,+Inc+%28Mobile+Massage%29/@25.8591251,-80.1203349

team_note: Reviews name at least 3 practicing therapists for AzuLux: Leticia (Diana), Natalia, and Omar, consistently across multiple 5-star reviews describing in-home/in-condo couples and individual massages in Miami Beach.
leticia_separate_practice_note: A HealthProfs listing for 'Leticia M Diana' (license MA49617, 20 years practicing, also an acupuncturist with FL license AP4677) lists AzuLux Sea Spa as her PRIMARY location but also lists a second, separate location ('The Sifre Center', 4014 Chase Avenue, Miami Beach) with her own $195/session acupuncture pricing. That pricing and that second location belong to Leticia's individual acupuncture practice, NOT to AzuLux Sea Spa's mobile massage service reviewed on Google -- deliberately NOT used as AzuLux pricing to avoid misattributing one practitioner's separate rates to the whole team-based business.
services_source: Reviews only (no published menu/prices anywhere found): 1-hour massage (solo and couples), lymphatic massage, deep tissue massage, in-home/in-condo service across Miami Beach. No prices published by the business on any source checked (Google, Birdeye, MassageBook, HealthProfs only shows Leticia's unrelated acupuncture rate). Per the adapted-variant rule this would have been 'se cotiza, escribenos' framing with NO invented price list, had photos allowed a build.

photos.curation_note: 0 of 7 available photos qualify for a premium gallery per the no-text-overlay / no-stock-photo rule. All are 2010s-style promotional flyers or staged brand photography, not real documentation of the team's actual work or premises. This is below the FORGE-BRIEF minimum of 5 real, own, non-stock photos required to build. No Instagram or Facebook account exists to source alternative real photos from (confirmed by WebSearch). HealthProfs has one professional headshot of therapist Leticia M Diana, but that is a personal headshot for her separate acupuncture practice, not AzuLux Sea Spa documentation, and a single headshot would not clear the 5-photo minimum regardless.

notes: Research performed via: node scripts/gmaps_detail.js, gmaps_reviews.js and gmaps_photocycle.js against the exact Google Maps place URL given in the task brief; curl domain probes on azulux.com (confirmed expired/parked, not live); WebSearch for social media and for the practitioners by name; WebFetch/curl on the Birdeye, MassageBook and HealthProfs listings that WebSearch surfaced. No data invented. Marked failed solely on the photo-minimum rule; every other dimension of this business (real reviews, real phone, real former domain, real named therapists, real credentials) was fully verifiable and documented above for a future attempt if better photos ever surface (e.g. if the business posts to a new Instagram, or if Leticia provides work photos directly).
